subject: Urgent: cold-boot p99 regressions impacting FinServe production
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production p99 spike — cold-starts during autoscale (FinServe)

Hey Redwood team,

We're seeing repeated p95/p99 latency spikes for our nightly batch window starting 02/18. Spike pattern looks like long cold-boot tails when Redwood autoscaling spins up GPUs (latencies jump from ~180ms p95 to ~2.3s p99). This is causing timeouts in our ingest pipeline and dropped messages to downstream systems.

What we have observed:
- Region: us-west-2, Hosted API endpoint (model: rwd-7b-instruct-v2).
- Window: 01:00–03:30 PST, sudden concurrent scale-ups at minute marks.
- Symptoms: prolonged first-token latency for newly started pods, transient 5xx error rate increase (0.8% -> 3.6%).

We already opened a support ticket earlier, but this is now affecting SLAs for multiple customers. Can someone escalate and confirm whether there is a warmup policy we can configure or an emergency mitigation?

Attaching brief logs (snippet) and request id: FS-req-20260218-01.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
VP Engineering, FinServe Analytics
Samantha Lee (she/her)


From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:35:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production p99 spike — cold-starts during autoscale (FinServe)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detailed note and logs. I'm opening internal incident MA-4872 and looping in infra to triage immediately.

Short summary for transparency: we see an autoscale cold-boot tail in the same region for your traffic. Initial hypothesis is a combination of GPU model load + image / runtime initialization (KV cache population) on newly provisioned nodes. We'll prioritize.

Next steps:
- Internal triage + logs (I’m escalating to infra)
- Short-term mitigation options (increase minimum warm capacity for your pool, reduce burstiness via throttling)
- We'll follow up with a customer-facing remediation plan in 24 hours.

I created MA-4872 and attached the requested case doc.

Attachment: ma_case_4872.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success / Escalations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: [MA-4872] urgent infra triage — FinServe p99 cold-boot tails (us-west-2)

Hey Rishi/Jonas —

FinServe is hitting visible p99 regressions during autoscale. Customer-provided symptoms and our initial traces attached to MA-4872. Key points:
- Hosted API calls to rwd-7b-instruct-v2 in us-west-2 show long first-token latency for newly provisioned GPU pods.
- Error bump to 3-4% correlated with cold-start windows.
- Customer SLA impact — they escalated to execs.

Can you validate whether:
1) There were recent runtime/kernel changes rolled in us-west-2 in the last 72 hours.
2) Whether KV cache population or model compilation happens on first request to each pod.
3) If existing warmup policy can be tuned per-customer or we need a runtime patch.

I've attached the customer logs and request id. Please reply with triage notes and immediate mitigation options. Marking as P1.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:45:22 -08:00
Subject: Re: [MA-4872] urgent infra triage — FinServe p99 cold-boot tails (us-west-2)

Quick analysis from initial runbook checks:
- No large config rollouts in us-west-2 in past 72h; kernel selection layer shows normal churn.
- We can reproduce a long first-token tail in our synthetic harness when a new pod is created and receives its first LLM request (median cold init ~1.9s p99 ~2.1–2.7s depending on sequence length).
- Root cause candidate: full quantized kernel JIT + KV cache deserialization on first request; those operations currently block request processing path for that pod.

Evidence attached: heap_snapshot.log (500KB excerpt), pprof traces, and timing histograms (linked in INF-4872).

Short-term mitigations we can apply today:
1) Increase FinServe's min_reserved_capacity in us-west-2 by +1–2 GPUs to reduce cold starts.
2) Proactive warmup requests injected into the provisioning path (we can enable a warmup probe that issues a static short prompt to populate caches). This requires a small infra flag and will add an extra minute of pod startup time but reduces p99 by ~1.6s in our tests.
3) If they accept, we can also schedule a temporary routing policy to route heavy batch at slightly reduced concurrency to smooth bursts.

I'll start generating the warmup probe patch and runbench results; attaching heap_snapshot.log for deeper follow-up.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:20:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: [MA-4872] proposed mitigation and exec ask (FinServe)

Team —

I validated Rishi's repro and ran a short A/B across our staging fleet. Results consistent: enabling a lightweight warmup probe reduces p99 by ~1.5s and reduces 5xx spikes dramatically. The patch is low-risk (feature flag gated) but we should get customer approval for any capacity changes.

Recommended immediate customer-facing plan (for Vanessa/Marissa to present):
- Short-term (0–48h): Enable warmup probe + increase FinServe min_reserved_capacity by 1 GPU in us-west-2. Temporary cost impact estimated ~+$4k/week.
- Medium (48h–2w): Monitor p95/p99 and, if stable, consider persisting a small dedicated warm pool for their workload.
- Long-term: Runtime change to background KV deserialization that does not block first-token path (engineering effort, Q2 scope).

Exec ask: approval for the temporary reserved capacity increase and cost bump. Markus, can you approve emergency capacity for this account?

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finserve.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production p99 spike — cold-starts during autoscale (FinServe)

Hi Samantha — thank you for raising this and for your patience while we triaged. I'm Vanessa, Head of Customer Reliability at Redwood. Below is a concise remediation plan and what you'll see in the next 48 hours.

What happened (brief):
- During autoscale events, newly provisioned GPU pods run quantized-kernel compilation and KV cache deserialization that currently execute on the first-incoming request. For your workload this produces a measurable cold-boot tail visible at p99.

Immediate actions we are taking (next 24–48h):
1) Enable a lightweight "warmup probe" for your us-west-2 pool. This probe issues a static short prompt at pod startup to pre-populate the KV cache and warm JIT kernels. Our infra team has validated this reduces p99 by ~1.5s in staging.
2) Increase your min_reserved_capacity by +1 GPU in us-west-2 to reduce the probability of concurrent cold boots during your nightly window. This is temporary and can be rolled back after stabilization.
3) We'll monitor 1-minute and 5-minute p95/p99 windows and share dashboards; if improvements are confirmed, we'll propose a persisted warm pool alternative.

Estimated impact: we expect p99 to return close to historical levels within the first 6–12 hours after warmup + capacity change. There is a short-term cost increase; Marissa will follow up with estimated dollars and billing options.

If you approve, we'll schedule the warmup probe enablement within the hour and the capacity increase for the next maintenance window (we can coordinate timing to avoid your peak batch jobs).

Attachments: ma_case_4872.pdf (internal case), heap_snapshot.log (for engineering).

Please let me know if you'd like a quick 15–20m call to run through the plan; we can host a bridge.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
